name: archive-channel
subject: American life 1930s-1980s told with public-domain archive film

schedule._note: Tue and Fri 12:00 America/New_York, confirmed by the owner 2026-11-03

voice._wpm: speaking pace while the narrator talks; film breaks come on top

text_llm._note: the key GROQ_API_KEY_AR is the owner's Groq key shared with the other channels, so this channel takes a model none of them uses: Closed Tabs and What If use openai/gpt-oss-120b, the dinosaurs qwen/qwen3.8-27b (checked 2026-11-03; the key serves gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b, qwen3.8-27b, allam-2-7b)

thumbnail.sharpest_frame: of the frames within 1.5 s of the chosen moment, the one with the highest variance of the Laplacian
thumbnail.source: the film's highest real resolution (pipeline/archive.files), never a 512Kb derivative
thumbnail.upscale: Real-ESRGAN realesr-general-x4v3 on the CPU (thumbnail frame only)
thumbnail.sharp_min: pipeline/thumbnail.py SHARP_MIN (336x189) and SHARP_MIN_FULL (1280x720), photo half

breathing._rule: The narrator does not talk without a break: 20-30% of the running time has no voice, in film breaks of 3-8 s where the chronicle's own sound, music and atmosphere carry the picture - on the most vivid shots and between chapters (owner, 02.11).

niche.rule: Every episode shows what things cost in its years next to what that is now, in today's dollars (US BLS CPI-U), with big price tags on screen.

prices.rule: A price in the hook, at least 6 price tags in the episode, and never more than 6 minutes without one: the price then, and now in the last full year's dollars. Only prices the sources state, with their year. The conversion is pipeline/prices.py (amount x CPI-U(today) / CPI-U(year)); the text model writes [price A Y | label] and [today A Y], never the sum of today.
prices.cpi_source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted
prices.on_screen: pipeline/cards.price_png: then, = now TODAY, 'in YYYY dollars - US BLS CPI-U', on the side of the shot with no face
prices._why: per chapter was tried first (2026-11-03): episode 1's sources state prices for 5 of its 9 chapters, and a price without a source is not allowed
